comparison: Perfect alignment on claim set (C1, C2, C17, C23-C29, C46) regarding burial evidence. Both evaluations are UNCERTAIN. OpenEval focuses on taphonomic evidence ruling out natural transport but notes burial interpretation relies on inference and dating uncertainties. Peer reviewers emphasize that validity depends entirely on adequacy of evidence in associated papers (Berger et al. 2023, 2024), which remain actively questioned.

High overlap on brain size measurements (C3-C6, C77-C78, C88). Both SUPPORTED. OpenEval validates endocranial volume data and comparative claims as well-documented. Peer reviewers do not challenge anatomical data, treating it as factual background. OpenEval explicitly notes appropriate scientific caution in acknowledging sampling limitations.

Partial overlap on cognitive inferences (C18-C19, C33-C34, C40). OpenEval is UNCERTAIN, noting collaboration/planning claims are reasonable but artificial light necessity is correlational and psychological extrapolations are speculative. Peer reviewers are also UNCERTAIN, with validity conditional on underlying behavioral claims from associated papers, which they find inadequate.

Strong overlap on cave navigation claims (C30-C32, C35-C39). OpenEval is UNCERTAIN about psychological extrapolations to H. naledi despite supporting anatomical advantages. Peer reviewers are SUPPORTED, not challenging cave navigation challenges or H. naledi anatomy, treating these as contextual information based on published studies.

High overlap on archaeological evidence for meaning-making behaviors (C7-C16, C41-C43, C48-C49, C60-C61). OpenEval is SUPPORTED, citing extensive archaeological documentation. Peer reviewers are UNCERTAIN, acknowledging the paper presents supporting evidence but emphasizing these claims must be adequately established given inadequate analyses in accompanying papers.

Strong overlap on behavioral complexity preceding brain size increase (C64-C65, C67, C69-C74, C83-C84). Both SUPPORTED. OpenEval validates evolutionary logic and temporal/volumetric data. Peer reviewers do not challenge these archaeological and paleontological facts, treating them as established context based on published data.

Moderate overlap on brain organization claims (C85-C86, C89-C90, C123). Both SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes frontal lobe organization evidence from endocast studies but acknowledges functional significance remains inferential. Peer reviewers support this perspective, noting research has focused on brain wiring to understand behavioral variability.

Strong overlap on theoretical framework challenging encephalization models (C91-C95, C117-C119). OpenEval is UNCERTAIN, noting the framework involves substantial speculation about conscious emotional awareness that cannot be directly tested. Peer reviewer R2 is also UNCERTAIN, directly challenging the framing and noting brain size emphasis is misplaced given rich research on other factors.

Overlap on conscious emotional awareness claims (C111-C114). OpenEval is UNCERTAIN, stating these claims extrapolate far beyond what mortuary behavior can demonstrate. Peer reviewers are also UNCERTAIN, noting cognitive implications rest on accepting behavioral evidence, which they find inadequately established in accompanying papers.

High overlap on comparative emotional cognition claims (C96-C110). Both SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these are well-supported by psychological and neuroscience literature, representing established knowledge rather than novel findings. Peer reviewers do not challenge these claims, treating them as established background context.

Strong overlap on fire antiquity and cave use comparisons (C53-C59). Both SUPPORTED. OpenEval validates claims about fire antiquity, association with multiple hominin species, and Neanderthal cave use comparisons. Peer reviewers do not challenge these comparative archaeological claims, treating them as factual context.

OpenEval evaluates comparative primate behavior claims (C20-C22) as SUPPORTED based on behavioral studies. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these claims appear to be treated as uncontroversial background context.

OpenEval is UNCERTAIN about phylogenetic position and fire use speculation (C47, C75-C76). Phylogenetic claims are supported but fire use by H. naledi ancestors is acknowledged speculation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates sex determination and brain size inference (C79-C80) as SUPPORTED based on cited literature and dimorphism patterns. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval is UNCERTAIN about Neanderthal cave use comparisons and tool symmetry claims (C115-C116), noting these involve inferential leaps about emotional states and are explicitly speculative. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
